entry.title: IceCube Nobel Prize
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Royal Swedish Academy of Science announced on 6 October that the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics goes to Francis Halzen, principal investigator of IceCube. The citation is for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. KM3NeT congratulated Halzen, and Physics World covered the award and discussed it in a podcast.

entry.title: Diffuse supernova neutrinos
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Super-Kamiokande reports an indication of electron antineutrinos from the diffuse supernova neutrino background, from a spectral fit of a 5003.0-day dataset. The analysis improves the rejection of atmospheric-neutrino backgrounds, the evaluation of systematic uncertainties and the fitting method. With a representative model the best-fit flux is 3.6 (+1.6, -1.5) cm^-2 s^-1 for E_ν > 13.3 MeV, a 2.6σ tension with the null hypothesis. Models with different spectral shapes give similar significances.

entry.title: Reactor CEvNS on germanium
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. CONUS+ reports what it calls the most precise measurement to date of reactor-antineutrino coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering. With 1296 kg·days of reactor-on exposure, a blind likelihood analysis gives 1555 ± 152 events at 10.2σ, within 0.6 standard deviations of the Standard Model expectation of 1701 ± 198. The same data give sin²θ_W = 0.225 ± 0.022 at a momentum transfer of about 10 MeV. A companion paper presents the run 2 analysis, covering detector characterisation, the background model and the signal prediction, after three of the original 1 kg detectors were replaced by larger 2.42 kg diodes.

entry.title: SBND long-lived particles
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A new paper searches for long-lived particles produced by neutrino-nucleus upscattering that decay to visible final states. It uses a subset of the SBND Cosmic Ray Tagger that ran as a standalone Beam Telescope in 2017-2018 on the Booster Neutrino Beam. Neutrino data taking with the full SBND detector began in December 2024.

entry.title: PUEO balloon payload
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The PUEO collaboration presents the design and flight of a balloon-borne antenna array. It is built to detect the Askaryan emission from ultrahigh-energy neutrino interactions. The motivation is that neutrinos at these energies carry information on cosmic-ray acceleration and propagation, but need very large detector volumes because the predicted flux is low.

entry.title: Baikal-GVD point sources
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Baikal-GVD is a cubic-kilometre-scale detector under construction in Lake Baikal, now 70% complete. A search for point-like astrophysical sources in a 5-year track-like dataset from 2019-2024 found no significant source. Upper limits are given for selected candidate objects and compared with results from IceCube, ANTARES and KM3NeT.

entry.title: Jinping geoneutrino prediction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A new preprint refines the geoneutrino flux prediction for the 500-tonne Jinping Neutrino Experiment. It builds a local crustal model at 0.2° × 0.2° resolution from a seismic velocity model and combines it with CRUST1.0. It also computes the inverse beta decay spectrum, including the reactor antineutrino background, for an assumed exposure of 500 t × 1500 days.

entry.title: The paper computes the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron-star matter containing Δ isob
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper computes the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron-star matter containing Δ isobars. It notes that this contribution had not been evaluated explicitly, although the nucleonic and hyperonic Urca processes are known as dominant cooling mechanisms. It is relevant to anyone using neutrino emission to model neutron-star thermal evolution.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is blind to a Majorana phase in two-flavour oscillations. It also shows that a rate anisotropy can supply an environmental phase reference, which gives the phase a cosine dependence in the exact finite-time result. This sets a clear condition for when open-system effects could in principle reveal a Majorana phase.

entry.title: The paper uses a gauged U(1) Lμ-Lτ model with an ultralight vector boson that mixes kinetically with the photo
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper uses a gauged U(1) Lμ-Lτ model with an ultralight vector boson that mixes kinetically with the photon. The boson generates an extra matter potential in the Sun and so modifies MSW flavour conversion. The author uses solar neutrino measurements from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande and discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD.

entry.title: The paper studies neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, with a scalar
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, with a scalar quadruplet and two vectorlike fermion triplets. Neutrino masses arise from a dimension-7 operator at tree level and a dimension-5 operator at one loop, so sub-eV masses are possible with a TeV-scale new-physics scale. The authors examine whether thermal leptogenesis is viable, noting that it differs from the canonical seesaw case.

entry.title: The paper asks whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected as nuclear reco
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper asks whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected as nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals (paleodetectors). It varies neutron-star mass and the nuclear equation of state, and includes failed supernovae that form black holes. It quantifies how sensitivity grows for models with larger neutrino emission.

entry.title: The paper proposes that the coalescence of degenerate helium cores in red giant collisions is a new class of t
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proposes that the coalescence of degenerate helium cores in red giant collisions is a new class of transient high-energy neutrino source. Using stellar models and hydrodynamic simulations, it builds a semianalytical estimate of the energy release, the magnetic-field amplification and the resulting neutrino flux. The authors find that the TeV-PeV signal may contribute to the diffuse IceCube flux.
